summary: Masayuki Tsukimoto specializes in Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Massimo Pallottino was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1927–1931). He later held posts at the University of Cagliari (~1945–1947) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1947–1980).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Masumi Mochizuki held posts at Minobusan University, serving as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and specially appointed professor (attested 2026).

Mathew Varghese works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held appointments at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, serving as a research fellow in 2012 and as a lecturer attested in 2026.

Mathieu Beaudouin studied at Panthéon-Sorbonne University and INALCO (PhD 2018–2023). A specialist in linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology, his appointments include INALCO (2018–2023), EPHE (2023–2025), and a British Academy International Fellowship at the University of Cambridge (2025).

Mathieu Boisvert specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He founded Université du Québec à Montréal, where he became a professor in 1992.
Mathilde Deromps was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Jules Bloch from 1911 to 1914.

Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Indology. He served as a librarian at Humboldt University of Berlin (1697) and as librarian and antiquary at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1697–1739).

Matteo Bartoli studied at Vienna (PhD ~1894–1898), Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann, Paris, and under Michele Kerbaker. A linguist, he held posts at the University of Pisa (1907–1908) and served as Professor of Linguistics at Turin (1908–1946).

Matthew Atmore Sherring studied at Coward College (~1847–1851) and University College London (1848–1850). Specializing in Indology and religious studies, he served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society from 1852.

Matthew B. Orsborn completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong (–2012) under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa, also studying under Hsing Yun and Huishang. In 2026, he is attested as professor at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Matthew Clark specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at SOAS University of London (PhD 1999–2004) under Daud Ali and George Botterill.
Matthew Immergut, who studied under Culadasa, works in Buddhist studies. He is attested in 2011 as an associate professor of sociology at Purchase College, State University of New York.

Matthew MacKenzie, a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies, completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1996–2004) and became an assistant professor of philosophy at Colorado State University in 2008.

Matthew R. Sayers studied Indology and religious studies at the University of Texas at Austin, completing his PhD under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle (attested 2008). He held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, the Inter-University Center, Osaka City University, and Duke University (PhD attested 2015). Supervised by Helen Baroni, Michel Mohr, and Richard M. Jaffe, his fields are Buddhist studies and Japanology.

Matthew T. Kapstein studied at UC Berkeley and Brown (PhD 1980–1987). Working in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, he held posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University (~1989–1996), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2002).
Matthew Thomson Adam worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a missionary teacher for the London Missionary Society (1820–1830) and taught at Presidency University until 1830.

Matthew W. King works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under Frances Garrett, Khenpo Kunga Sherab, and Thubten Champa, earning his PhD from the University of Toronto by 2014.

Matthias Alexander Castrén studied linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies at the University of Helsinki and Imperial Alexander University (~1830–1836). He later held posts at both institutions from ~1840 to 1852.
